item.title: AI as cultural technology: judgments that travel
item.description:
Vale and Mara develop a perspective on AI as cultural technology through four readings: Kommers and colleagues on computational hermeneutics; Yiu, Kosoy, and Gopnik on cultural transmission and innovation; Collier on a world without work; and Robbins on educational assessment. They compare claims, evidence, and limitations, trace historical connections, and offer separate takeaways on portable judgments, recognition, and unfamiliar possibilities. Duration: 8:51. Chapters: 0:00 Overview; 0:58 Grounded encounters; 4:58 Genealogies; 7:42 What is interesting now.

Sources (APA)

  • Kommers, C., et al. (2026). Computational hermeneutics: Evaluating generative AI as a cultural technology. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 9, 1753041. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2026.1753041
  • Yiu, E., Kosoy, E., & Gopnik, A. (2024). Transmission Versus Truth, Imitation Versus Innovation: What Children Can Do That Large Language and Language-and-Vision Models Cannot (Yet). Perspectives on Psychological Science, 19(5), 874–883. https://doi.org/10.1177/17456916231201401
  • Collier, C. (2026, September 2). We already know what a world without work looks like. Asterisk Magazine. https://asteriskmag.substack.com/p/we-already-know-what-a-world-without
  • Robbins, H. (2026, July 29). The Miasma Theory of Education. Anecdotal Value. https://hollisrobbinsanecdotal.substack.com/p/the-miasma-theory-of-education

item.title: Inside Latent Space: Brains, GANs, and Finnegans Wake
item.description:
This episode closely follows Begus and Begus (2026) to explain latent space as both a computational structure and an interpretable interior. We walk through their three linked case studies, clarify why they chose their methods and corpora, and assess why their conclusion about AI interiors matters.

Sources (APA)

  • Begus, N., Begus, G. (2026). Latent Spacecraft: Brains, GANs, Finnegans. Antikythera. https://doi.org/10.1162/ANTI.5KPI

Featured Notes

  • Latent spaces are abstract, organized structures of vectors with hundreds or thousands of dimensions, created by training procedures for further operationalization.
  • FiwGAN [Featural InfoWaveGAN] and ciwGAN [Categorical InfoWave GAN] are, for now, the only deep neural architecture with baked-in production and perception.
  • Toward an Architecture of Latent Spaces: In attempting to make the latent space more legible, and thus narratable, than it currently is, what direction should we choose?
  • 16 code variables in the latent space, a learning rate of 10^-5, six convolutional layers and 65,536 outputs that correspond to approximately 4 s of audio at 16 kHz sampling rate.
  • Conclusion: Interior and Exterior in AI cultures: We are mostly seeing end products, final outcomes, exteriors.

item.title: A Perspectival Moral History of the Novel: What LLMs Can and Cannot Tell Us
item.description:
This episode examines Andrew Piper’s 2025 study on using large language models to extract story morals from thousands of Wikipedia plot summaries of modern novels. The script stays close to Piper’s claims: the project is interpretive rather than taxonomic, uses prompt variation to test model sensitivity, and treats moral extraction as a perspectival workflow shaped by language, archive, model, and researcher. It also marks where broader implications are inferred rather than directly claimed.

Sources (APA)

  • Piper, A. (2025). Towards a Perspectival Moral History of the Novel Using LLMs. Journal of Computational Literary Studies. https://doi.org/10.48694/jcls.4168

Featured Notes

  • The paper frames a "many-to-many relationship" among wikiplots across language editions, highlighting perspectival differences in what gets summarized and how.
  • The project links story morals to narratological schema traditions (for example, Campbell, Frye, Genette, Propp, Thompson) while shifting focus from "what happened" to "why this was told."
  • Methods note: the prompt asks for a single-sentence moral, then three keywords, with a fallback of NONE if information is insufficient.
  • Data note: the study uses 9,756 human-written English Wikipedia story summaries of books published since the start of the twentieth century.

item.title: Everything Is Television: Flow, Attention, and the New Media Attractor
item.description:
A fidelity-style walkthrough of Derek Thompson’s 2025 essay arguing that major media formats are converging toward continuous short-form video “flow,” with implications for social life, attention, and political culture. The script distinguishes Thompson’s claims, his cited evidence, and clearly labeled derived inferences.

Sources (APA)

  • Thompson, D. (2025). Everything Is Television. https://www.derekthompson.org/p/why-everything-became-television

Featured Notes

  • A spooky convergence is happening in media.
  • Whether the starting point is a student directory (Facebook), radio, or an AI image generator, the end point seems to be the same: a river of short-form video.
  • In his 1974 book Television: Technology and Cultural Form, Raymond Williams: wrote that “in all communications systems before [television], the essential items were discrete.”
  • 300 hours a year to learn a new skill, or participate in their community, or have more children.
